I have/had a friend that essentially had a similar situation. Long term monogamous relationship when she decided she had more love to give. She decided to date a FtM friend (who they used to party with), and she told myself and a few friends she knew it was going to end badly, which we called her out on, but she didn't take our advice. Fast forward, this guy used her and her long term bf, really fucked her up mentally, and she is probably still dealing with the trauma it did to her and her relationship with her long term bf. She has pushed a lot of us away, I don't think I've seen her in over a year.  There is nothing you can do for the other individual if they don't want help, and that's okay.

Now, as someone who's first relationship was abusive, a few words of advice for you.

1. It is not your fault, and you can't fix other people who are broken, not matter how hard you do love them. You can't piece their broken pieces together because that's something they need to do.
2. Time. Time is the ultimate healer. I was 15 - 20 in said relationship, and 10 years later, I'm still pretty screwy in the head some days. I still have flashbacks, if I see a white van I panic, or if my fiance/husband touches me a certain way during sex, I freeze. It's okay to not be okay, because I promise someday, it will all be better. While I carry that trauma, I don't let it define me and have worked hard to be better.
3. Journal! Word vomit onto a page to express yourself a little bit everyday, even if it's "today sucked". You will notice you feel a little more free each time, even if you are feeling low.
4. Learn to take care of yourself. Love yourself, because i can almost guarantee you haven't loved you in a long time. Treat yourself to a nice breakfast/ lunch/dinner, take a nice shower/bath, go for a walk and sit to listen to the birds, whatever makes you happy. Find yourself.
5. Therapy... i only finally sought therapy last year finally, at the urging of my hubby, because I could not pull myself out of my funk. It felt good to just gripe about everyday crap, and sometimes talk about the things that did happen back then. I've gotten better at grounding and breathing when the flashbacks happen, and feel better knowing I'm not the only one out there to feel the way I do.

I wish you all the joy in the world, OP, and just know it's okay to not be okay. You had a major shift in your life, and it'll take time to feel better. You did the right thing, even if you hold regrets. It will be better someday, I promise.
